title: The summary that invented a quarter
blurb: Chunk counters could commit without their summaries.
prompt: A board summary invented a revenue decline because the draft appended a partial rolling summary that claimed chunks it never processed, and a source edit silently reused an old summary. Review it, fix it, and prove progress is atomic and content-bound.
aiNote: The draft commits the rolling summary and its chunk counter as separate writes, so a crash can produce a summary that claims coverage it never had, and its cache key omits the source content hash, so an edited source resumes and extends the previous summary.
testIdea: Crash between counter and summary writes and assert the reopened summary lists only completed chunks; edit the source and assert a new summary line starts; request a summary for a foreign tenant and assert 404.
followUps: How would you structure summaries so citations survive edits?
What compression ratio warns you a summary is probably extractive?
When is a trimmed extract better than an abstractive summary?
